blocks.x: The stack is boring by design — proven components, no experimental dependencies:

items: Openshift As The Hybrid Runtime Standard
One runtime standard across data center and cloud — operations learns it once.
Ansible
Configuration as reviewed code for the estates scripts cannot reach.
Openshift Ai
Model lifecycle on the same governed runtime the estate already runs.
Selinux And Sc Security Profiles As Defaults
Hardening shipped as the default profile, not as a hardening project.
Enterprise Linux Discipline Under Every Workload
Supported, patched, pinned bases under everything — boring infrastructure on purpose.
streaming ingest
Events land in seconds, not overnight batches — the precondition for decisions that happen in the moment.
dbt transformation graph
Tested, documented models with lineage exposure — the transform layer your analysts can actually read.
cost-aware clustering
Workloads land on the cheapest compute that still meets the latency budget.
freshness SLOs
Data age treated like uptime — a budget, an owner and an alert when it slips.

blocks.x: The joint pattern for Red Hat Alliance: our pod does the build, your named owners hold the gates, and the evidence is generated in systems your teams already operate.
The quarter-close package, built to be handed over rather than demonstrated:

items: Joint architecture pack
The target architecture drawn against your estate, with interfaces and owners made explicit.
Certified delivery pod
A named team with the clearances your estate requires — the same people from diagnosis to handover.
Support map
Who answers when something breaks — named roles, response expectations and the escalation path.

blocks.x: Ask for the Red Hat reference pack — or bring your use case to a joint working session with both platform teams.
